function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

coverage_root_uris.description: Deprecated and ignored: coverage is always collected for the packages under test.

name_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against test item names.

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

items.description: Specific test item ids to run, as reported by julia_list_testitems. If omitted, runs all (or filtered) items.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Re-run only the failed and errored Julia test items from an earlier run, reusing that run's settings. Returns a new test run id; the original run is left intact. The usual loop is julia_run_testitems, fix the code, then this — the worker processes pick up the fix via Revise. Waits up to max_wait_seconds like julia_run_testitems and returns early with status "running" the same way.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_rerun_failed

timeout.description: Per-item timeout override.

max_workers.description: Max workers override.

max_wait_seconds.description: Override for how long this call waits before returning the run as still running (default 600).

testrun_id.description: ID of the previous test run whose failures to re-run.

memory_threshold.description: Worker recycle threshold override.

function.description: Stop an in-progress Julia test run — typically one julia_run_testitems handed back with status "running" because it outlasted max_wait_seconds, or one that turned out to be hanging. function.description: Get the summary and per-item status lines for a Julia test run, whether it has completed or is still going — this is the tool to poll after julia_run_testitems returned with status "running". include_passing.description: Include passing test items in results (default: false).

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run.

function.description: Get the full result of one or more Julia test items: failure messages, stack traces, and captured output (stdout and stderr interleaved). function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testitem_detail

testitem_ids.description: Test item ids to inspect. Unknown ids are reported per item rather than failing the call.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on captured output per item (default 8000). The tail is kept; read the testrun://{id}/items/{id}/output resource for the full stream.

max_messages.description: Cap on failure messages per item (default 20).

testrun_id.description: Test run ID.

testitem_id.description: Single test item id. Prefer testitem_ids for more than one.

max_stack_frames.description: Cap on stack frames per message (default 20).

function.description: List every Julia test run this server has started, with status and pass/fail counts. Use it to recover a testrun_id for julia_get_testrun_results, julia_get_testitem_detail or julia_rerun_failed — including when a julia_run_testitems call was interrupted or its result went missing. Runs that outlasted max_wait_seconds show as "running" until they finish or are cancelled.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_testruns

function.description: List the Julia worker processes currently held for running test items. They persist between runs by design — that is what makes repeat runs fast. Read the testprocess://{process_id}/output resource for a process's raw output, which is where precompilation and startup failures show up.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_test_processes

function.description: Kill a Julia test worker process. Its loaded packages and compiled code are lost, so the next run needing it pays full Julia startup and precompilation again. Only worth doing when a worker is wedged or Revise cannot apply a change — editing a struct definition, for instance.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_terminate_test_process

function.description: Get line-level Julia code coverage for a test run. Only available for runs started with mode="Coverage"; anything else returns an error.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_coverage_results

testrun_id.description: Test run ID (must have been run with mode="Coverage").

function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. State — variables, functions, loaded packages, compiled code — survives across julia_eval_code calls, so iterating inside one session avoids paying Julia's startup and compilation cost over and over. Prefer this over shelling out to `julia -e` for anything beyond a single throwaway command. Revise is loaded, so edits made to package source on disk take effect on the next evaluation without a restart. Sessions are independent of the analysis workspace: julia_set_workspace_folders is not required. The response echoes the resolved environment; pass it back here to replace a session that died.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_create_session

use_test_env.description: Activate the package's test environment via TestEnv (default false).

project.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the project to activate. Omitted means Julia's default environment.

package.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the package being developed, when there is one.

env.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes the variable.

package_name.description: Name of the package being developed.

julia_cmd.description: Path to the Julia executable (default: the one running this server).

function.description: Evaluate Julia code in a persistent session and return the value, captured output, and any error. A Julia exception comes back as a normal result with status "error" rather than a tool failure, so the message and backtrace are there to read. Definitions and variables persist for later calls in the same session. Revise runs first by default, so edits made to package source on disk are picked up before the code runs.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_eval_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the evaluation is interrupted. Omit for no timeout; Julia precompilation can take minutes.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on returned output, keeping the tail (default 8000).

revise.description: Run Revise first so edits made on disk take effect (default true).

session_id.description: Session to evaluate in, from julia_create_session.

code.description: Julia code to evaluate. Multiple top-level statements are allowed; the value of the last one is returned.

function.description: Interrupt whatever a Julia session is currently evaluating, as Ctrl-C would. Queued requests are discarded and the session stays alive and usable. Julia code that never yields (`while true; end`, or a long call into a C library) may not be interruptible, especially on Windows — julia_kill_session is the only recourse there.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_interrupt_session

function.description: Terminate a Julia session and discard all of its state. There is no restart tool: to start over with the same setup, call julia_create_session with the environment julia_list_sessions reports for it.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_kill_session

function.description: List the Julia sessions this server manages, with each one's status and the environment it was created with. That environment is what julia_create_session needs to recreate a session after julia_kill_session.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_sessions

function.description: Profile Julia code in a session and return the hottest functions by self and total sample count. Use kind="alloc" for an allocation profile instead of CPU sampling. Run the code once with julia_eval_code first — otherwise compilation dominates the samples and the profile says nothing useful.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_profile_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the profile run is interrupted.

max_entries.description: Number of hot functions to report (default 25).

code.description: Julia code to profile. Run it once first so compilation does not dominate the profile.

function.description: List the bindings of a module in a Julia session with rendered values — the equivalent of a debugger's variable pane. Values too expensive to render eagerly come back with lazy=true and an id; pass that id back as variable_id to expand that value's children.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_session_variables

include_modules.description: Include module bindings in the listing (default false).

variable_id.description: Expand the children of this lazily reported variable instead of listing a module.

- Be concise in your responses

function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.
function.name: bash

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.
function.name: edit

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.
function.name: write

content.description: Content to write to the file

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

function.description: Load Julia packages or projects into this server's workspace. This is a prerequisite for every other Julia workspace tool — julia_get_diagnostics, julia_format_file, julia_list_testitems and julia_run_testitems all fail until it has been called. Parses the Julia source under each folder, resolves the Project.toml/Manifest.toml environments, and detects @testitem and @testsetup blocks. The workspace then keeps itself up to date as files change on disk, so nothing needs to be called after editing a file. Calling this again replaces the previous configuration. Julia sessions (julia_create_session) are separate and need no workspace.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_set_workspace_folders

folders.description: Absolute paths of the Julia package or project folders to load, normally the repository roots being worked on.

watch_interval.description: Seconds between file system scans (default 1.0). The workspace always tracks the file system; this only tunes how quickly edits are noticed.

function.description: Report Julia syntax errors, lint warnings and test item detection errors, for the whole workspace or a single file. This is static analysis: no Julia code is run and nothing is compiled, so it is cheap enough to call after every edit. Prefer it over shelling out to julia to check whether a file parses. Results are grouped by file with 1-based line/column positions. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_diagnostics

path.description: Optional absolute file path or file:// URI. When omitted, diagnostics for the whole workspace are returned.

severity.description: Only report these severities, e.g. ["error"] or ["error", "warning"].

source.description: Only report diagnostics from these sources, e.g. ["JuliaSyntax.jl"] or ["StaticLint.jl"].

max_results.description: Maximum number of diagnostics to return (default 200). The response reports whether it was truncated.

wait_for_ready.description: Wait for environment-dependent analysis (package resolution) to finish first. Slower, but required for checks that need the surrounding environment, such as unresolved imports and missing references — without it those checks are silently absent.

function.description: Format Julia source code with the style configured by the nearest JuliaFormat.toml (JuliaFormatter by default, or Runic when style="runic"). Returns the text edits without touching disk; set apply=true to write them and refresh the workspace. A file the configuration excludes returns excluded=true with no edits rather than an error. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders, and only works on files inside the workspace.

path.description: Absolute file path or file:// URI of the file to format.

apply.description: Write the formatted result to disk and refresh the workspace. Defaults to false, which only returns the edits.

stop_line.description: Last line to format (1-based, inclusive). Requires start_line.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

# Least-squares slope of y against 1, 2, ..., n.
const DEFAULT_PATH = "data/measurements.txt"

function fit_slope(path = DEFAULT_PATH)
    y = parse.(Float64, readlines(path))
    n = length(y)
    xm = (n + 1) / 2
    ym = sum(y) / n
    return sum(((1:n) .- xm) .* (y .- ym)) / sum(((1:n) .- xm) .^ 2)
end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module Slugify

export slugify

function slugify(s::AbstractString)
    t = lowercase(Base.Unicode.normalize(s; stripmark = true))
    t = replace(t, r"[^a-z0-9]+" => "-")
    return strip(t, '-')
end

end

When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module MinHeap

export BinaryMinHeap

struct BinaryMinHeap{T}
    data::Vector{T}
end
BinaryMinHeap{T}() where {T} = BinaryMinHeap{T}(T[])

Base.length(h::BinaryMinHeap) = length(h.data)
Base.isempty(h::BinaryMinHeap) = isempty(h.data)

function Base.first(h::BinaryMinHeap)
    isempty(h) && throw(ArgumentError("heap is empty"))
    return h.data[1]
end

function Base.push!(h::BinaryMinHeap, x)
    d = h.data
    push!(d, x)
    i = length(d)
    while i > 1 && isless(d[i], d[i ÷ 2])
        d[i], d[i ÷ 2] = d[i ÷ 2], d[i]
        i ÷= 2
    end
    return h
end

function Base.pop!(h::BinaryMinHeap)
    isempty(h) && throw(ArgumentError("heap is empty"))
    d = h.data
    top = d[1]
    d[1] = d[end]
    pop!(d)
    i = 1
    while 2i <= length(d)
        l = 2i
        isless(d[l], d[i]) || break
        d[i], d[l] = d[l], d[i]
        i = l
    end
    return top
end

end

@testitem "heap sort agrees with sort" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(4)
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for _ in 1:200
        v = rand(rng, -20:20, rand(rng, 0:40))
        h = BinaryMinHeap{Int}()
        foreach(x -> push!(h, x), v)
        got = [pop!(h) for _ in 1:length(v)]
        if got != sort(v)
            bad[] = (v, got)
            break
        end
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

@testitem "interleaved pushes and pops match a sorted model" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(6)
    h = BinaryMinHeap{Float64}(); model = Float64[]
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for _ in 1:2000
        if isempty(model) || rand(rng) < 0.6
            x = round(randn(rng); digits = 1)
            push!(h, x); push!(model, x); sort!(model)
        else
            got, want = pop!(h), popfirst!(model)
            got == want || (bad[] = (got, want); break)
        end
        if !isempty(model) && first(h) != model[1]
            bad[] = (first(h), model[1])
            break
        end
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

@testitem "strings and errors" begin
    h = BinaryMinHeap{String}()
    foreach(w -> push!(h, w), ["été", "zebra", "apple", "日本", "Zoo"])
    @test [pop!(h) for _ in 1:5] == sort(["été", "zebra", "apple", "日本", "Zoo"])
    @test_throws "heap is empty" pop!(h)
    @test_throws "heap is empty" first(h)
end

@testitem "200_000 operations are fast" begin
    h = BinaryMinHeap{Int}()
    t = @elapsed begin
        for i in 1:200_000
            push!(h, (i * 7919) % 100_003)
        end
        for _ in 1:200_000
            pop!(h)
        end
    end
    @test t < 3
end

`BinaryMinHeap{T}` is in `/work/Project/MinHeap/src/MinHeap.jl`; all 6 test items pass.

The first run failed 3 of 6 items. `pop!` sifted down against the left child only, so a smaller right child stayed below a larger parent, and pops came out of order (for example `"zebra"` after `"été"`). The sift-down now picks the smaller of both children.

An empty result means the workspace does not use test items, in which case fall back to the package's own test entrypoint. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_testitems

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs (case-insensitive).

name_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against test item names (case-insensitive).

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

items.description: Filter to these specific test item ids.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

coverage_root_uris.description: Deprecated and ignored: coverage is always collected for the packages under test.

name_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against test item names.

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

items.description: Specific test item ids to run, as reported by julia_list_testitems. If omitted, runs all (or filtered) items.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Re-run only the failed and errored Julia test items from an earlier run, reusing that run's settings. Returns a new test run id; the original run is left intact. The usual loop is julia_run_testitems, fix the code, then this — the worker processes pick up the fix via Revise. Waits up to max_wait_seconds like julia_run_testitems and returns early with status "running" the same way.

timeout.description: Per-item timeout override.

max_workers.description: Max workers override.

max_wait_seconds.description: Override for how long this call waits before returning the run as still running (default 600).

testrun_id.description: ID of the previous test run whose failures to re-run.

memory_threshold.description: Worker recycle threshold override.

function.description: Stop an in-progress Julia test run — typically one julia_run_testitems handed back with status "running" because it outlasted max_wait_seconds, or one that turned out to be hanging. Items that have not finished are abandoned and their worker processes are killed; results already collected stay readable via julia_get_testrun_results. Errors if the run has already finished.

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run to cancel.

function.description: Get the summary and per-item status lines for a Julia test run, whether it has completed or is still going — this is the tool to poll after julia_run_testitems returned with status "running". It returns immediately with the current state; the run is done once status is no longer "running". Same compact shape julia_run_testitems returns — use julia_get_testitem_detail for failure messages, stack traces and captured output. Durations are milliseconds; the summary duration is elapsed wall-clock time, and for a run still in progress it is the time elapsed so far.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testrun_results

include_passing.description: Include passing test items in results (default: false).

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Get the full result of one or more Julia test items: failure messages, stack traces, and captured output (stdout and stderr interleaved). This is the follow-up to julia_run_testitems — pass every id you want to inspect in a single call rather than one call per item. Supply testitem_ids or testitem_id; at least one is required. If a whole worker process died before running anything (a precompilation error, say), the cause is in the testprocess://{process_id}/output resource instead.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testitem_detail

testitem_ids.description: Test item ids to inspect. Unknown ids are reported per item rather than failing the call.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on captured output per item (default 8000). The tail is kept; read the testrun://{id}/items/{id}/output resource for the full stream.

max_messages.description: Cap on failure messages per item (default 20).

testrun_id.description: Test run ID.

testitem_id.description: Single test item id. Prefer testitem_ids for more than one.

max_stack_frames.description: Cap on stack frames per message (default 20).

function.description: List every Julia test run this server has started, with status and pass/fail counts. Use it to recover a testrun_id for julia_get_testrun_results, julia_get_testitem_detail or julia_rerun_failed — including when a julia_run_testitems call was interrupted or its result went missing. Runs that outlasted max_wait_seconds show as "running" until they finish or are cancelled.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_testruns

function.description: List the Julia worker processes currently held for running test items. They persist between runs by design — that is what makes repeat runs fast. Read the testprocess://{process_id}/output resource for a process's raw output, which is where precompilation and startup failures show up.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_test_processes

function.description: Kill a Julia test worker process. Its loaded packages and compiled code are lost, so the next run needing it pays full Julia startup and precompilation again. Only worth doing when a worker is wedged or Revise cannot apply a change — editing a struct definition, for instance.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_terminate_test_process

function.description: Get line-level Julia code coverage for a test run. Only available for runs started with mode="Coverage"; anything else returns an error.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_coverage_results

testrun_id.description: Test run ID (must have been run with mode="Coverage").

function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. State — variables, functions, loaded packages, compiled code — survives across julia_eval_code calls, so iterating inside one session avoids paying Julia's startup and compilation cost over and over. Prefer this over shelling out to `julia -e` for anything beyond a single throwaway command. Revise is loaded, so edits made to package source on disk take effect on the next evaluation without a restart. Sessions are independent of the analysis workspace: julia_set_workspace_folders is not required. The response echoes the resolved environment; pass it back here to replace a session that died.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_create_session

use_test_env.description: Activate the package's test environment via TestEnv (default false).

project.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the project to activate. Omitted means Julia's default environment.

package.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the package being developed, when there is one.

env.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes the variable.

package_name.description: Name of the package being developed.

julia_cmd.description: Path to the Julia executable (default: the one running this server).

function.description: Evaluate Julia code in a persistent session and return the value, captured output, and any error. A Julia exception comes back as a normal result with status "error" rather than a tool failure, so the message and backtrace are there to read. Definitions and variables persist for later calls in the same session. Revise runs first by default, so edits made to package source on disk are picked up before the code runs.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_eval_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the evaluation is interrupted. Omit for no timeout; Julia precompilation can take minutes.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on returned output, keeping the tail (default 8000).

revise.description: Run Revise first so edits made on disk take effect (default true).

session_id.description: Session to evaluate in, from julia_create_session.

code.description: Julia code to evaluate. Multiple top-level statements are allowed; the value of the last one is returned.

function.description: Interrupt whatever a Julia session is currently evaluating, as Ctrl-C would. Queued requests are discarded and the session stays alive and usable. Julia code that never yields (`while true; end`, or a long call into a C library) may not be interruptible, especially on Windows — julia_kill_session is the only recourse there.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_interrupt_session

function.description: Terminate a Julia session and discard all of its state. There is no restart tool: to start over with the same setup, call julia_create_session with the environment julia_list_sessions reports for it.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_kill_session

function.description: List the Julia sessions this server manages, with each one's status and the environment it was created with. That environment is what julia_create_session needs to recreate a session after julia_kill_session.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_sessions

function.description: Profile Julia code in a session and return the hottest functions by self and total sample count. Use kind="alloc" for an allocation profile instead of CPU sampling. Run the code once with julia_eval_code first — otherwise compilation dominates the samples and the profile says nothing useful.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_profile_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the profile run is interrupted.

max_entries.description: Number of hot functions to report (default 25).

code.description: Julia code to profile. Run it once first so compilation does not dominate the profile.

function.description: List the bindings of a module in a Julia session with rendered values — the equivalent of a debugger's variable pane. Values too expensive to render eagerly come back with lazy=true and an id; pass that id back as variable_id to expand that value's children.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_session_variables

include_modules.description: Include module bindings in the listing (default false).

variable_id.description: Expand the children of this lazily reported variable instead of listing a module.

function.description: Load Julia packages or projects into this server's workspace. This is a prerequisite for every other Julia workspace tool — julia_get_diagnostics, julia_format_file, julia_list_testitems and julia_run_testitems all fail until it has been called. Parses the Julia source under each folder, resolves the Project.toml/Manifest.toml environments, and detects @testitem and @testsetup blocks. The workspace then keeps itself up to date as files change on disk, so nothing needs to be called after editing a file. Calling this again replaces the previous configuration. Julia sessions (julia_create_session) are separate and need no workspace.

function.description: Report Julia syntax errors, lint warnings and test item detection errors, for the whole workspace or a single file. module PeekIter

export Peekable, peek

import Base: peek

mutable struct Peekable{I}
    it::I
    state::Any
    started::Bool
    buf::Union{Nothing,Some{Any}}
end
Peekable(it) = Peekable(it, nothing, false, nothing)

function _advance!(p::Peekable)
    r = p.started ? iterate(p.it, p.state) : iterate(p.it)
    p.started = true
    isnothing(r) && return nothing
    p.state = r[2]
    return Some{Any}(r[1])
end

function peek(p::Peekable)
    isnothing(p.buf) && (p.buf = _advance!(p))
    return p.buf
end

function Base.iterate(p::Peekable, _ = nothing)
    v = _advance!(p)
    p.buf = nothing
    isnothing(v) && return nothing
    return something(v), nothing
end

Base.IteratorSize(::Type{<:Peekable}) = Base.SizeUnknown()

end

module TallyCount

export Counter, add!, remove!, total, most_common

struct Counter{K}
    counts::Dict{K,Int}
end
Counter{K}() where {K} = Counter{K}(Dict{K,Int}())

Base.length(c::Counter) = length(c.counts)
Base.getindex(c::Counter, key) = get(c.counts, key, 0)
total(c::Counter) = sum(values(c.counts); init = 0)

function add!(c::Counter, key, n::Integer = 1)
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot add a negative count ($n); use remove!"))
    n == 0 && return c
    c.counts[key] = get(c.counts, key, 0) + n
    return c
end

function remove!(c::Counter, key, n::Integer = 1)
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot remove a negative count ($n); use add!"))
    have = c[key]
    have >= n || throw(ArgumentError("cannot remove $n of $(repr(key)): only $have present"))
    if have == n
        delete!(c.counts, key)
    else
        c.counts[key] = have - n
    end
    return c
end

function most_common(c::Counter, k::Integer)
    k >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("k must be nonnegative, got $k"))
    ranked = sort!(collect(c.counts); by = kv -> (-kv.second, kv.first))
    return ranked[1:min(k, length(ranked))]
end

end

@testitem "basic operations and tie order" begin
    c = Counter{String}()
    for w in ["été", "日本", "été", "a", "b", "日本", "z"]
        add!(c, w)
    end
    @test c["été"] == 2 && c["nope"] == 0
    @test length(c) == 5 && total(c) == 7
    @test most_common(c, 3) == ["été" => 2, "日本" => 2, "a" => 1]
    @test most_common(c, 0) == []
    @test length(most_common(c, 99)) == 5
end

@testitem "remove! semantics" begin
    c = Counter{Int}()
    add!(c, 5, 3)
    remove!(c, 5, 2)
    @test c[5] == 1
    remove!(c, 5)
    @test length(c) == 0 && c[5] == 0
    @test_throws "only 0 present" remove!(c, 5)
    add!(c, 1, 2)
    @test_throws "cannot remove 3 of 1: only 2 present" remove!(c, 1, 3)
    @test_throws ArgumentError add!(c, 1, -1)
end

@testitem "random operations agree with a Dict model" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(1)
    c = Counter{Int}(); model = Dict{Int,Int}()
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for step in 1:3000
        k = rand(rng, 1:8)
        if rand(rng) < 0.55
            n = rand(rng, 0:3); add!(c, k, n); n > 0 && (model[k] = get(model, k, 0) + n)
        else
            n = rand(rng, 0:3)
            if get(model, k, 0) >= n
                remove!(c, k, n)
                m = get(model, k, 0) - n
                m == 0 ? delete!(model, k) : (model[k] = m)
            else
                threw = try
                    remove!(c, k, n)
                    false
                catch e
                    e isa ArgumentError || rethrow()
                    true
                end
                threw || (bad[] = (:no_throw, step); break)
            end
        end
        expected = sort(collect(model); by = kv -> (-kv[2], kv[1]))
        (c.counts == model && most_common(c, 3) == expected[1:min(3, end)] && total(c) == sum(values(model); init = 0)) ||
            (bad[] = (step, c.counts, model); break)
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module ModPow

export powmod

mulmod(a::Int64, b::Int64, m::Int64) = Int64(mod(widemul(a, b), m))

function powmod(b::Integer, e::Integer, m::Integer)
    e >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("exponent must be nonnegative, got $e"))
    m >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("modulus must be positive, got $m"))
    base = mod(Int64(b), Int64(m))
    result = Int64(1) % Int64(m)
    ex = Int64(e)
    mm = Int64(m)
    while ex > 0
        isodd(ex) && (result = mulmod(result, base, mm))
        base = mulmod(base, base, mm)
        ex >>= 1
    end
    return result
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. function.description: Interrupt whatever a Julia session is currently evaluating, as Ctrl-C would. Queued requests are discarded and the session stays alive and usable. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

module QuantileLite

export percentile

function percentile(x::AbstractVector{<:Real}, p::Real)
    isempty(x) && throw(ArgumentError("cannot take a percentile of an empty vector"))
    0 <= p <= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("p must be in [0, 1], got $p"))
    any(isnan, x) && return float(eltype(x))(NaN)
    s = sort!(x)
    n = length(s)
    h = (n - 1) * p + 1
    lo = floor(Int, h)
    hi = min(lo + 1, n)
    T = float(eltype(x))
    return T(s[lo] + (h - lo) * (s[hi] - s[lo]))
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Load Julia packages or projects into this server's workspace. This is a prerequisite for every other Julia workspace tool — julia_get_diagnostics, julia_format_file, julia_list_testitems and julia_run_testitems all fail until it has been called. Parses the Julia source under each folder, resolves the Project.toml/Manifest.toml environments, and detects @testitem and @testsetup blocks. The workspace then keeps itself up to date as files change on disk, so nothing needs to be called after editing a file. Calling this again replaces the previous configuration. Julia sessions (julia_create_session) are separate and need no workspace.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_set_workspace_folders

folders.description: Absolute paths of the Julia package or project folders to load, normally the repository roots being worked on.

watch_interval.description: Seconds between file system scans (default 1.0). The workspace always tracks the file system; this only tunes how quickly edits are noticed.

function.description: Report Julia syntax errors, lint warnings and test item detection errors, for the whole workspace or a single file. This is static analysis: no Julia code is run and nothing is compiled, so it is cheap enough to call after every edit. Prefer it over shelling out to julia to check whether a file parses. Results are grouped by file with 1-based line/column positions. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_diagnostics

path.description: Optional absolute file path or file:// URI. When omitted, diagnostics for the whole workspace are returned.

severity.description: Only report these severities, e.g. ["error"] or ["error", "warning"].

source.description: Only report diagnostics from these sources, e.g. ["JuliaSyntax.jl"] or ["StaticLint.jl"].

max_results.description: Maximum number of diagnostics to return (default 200). The response reports whether it was truncated.

wait_for_ready.description: Wait for environment-dependent analysis (package resolution) to finish first. Slower, but required for checks that need the surrounding environment, such as unresolved imports and missing references — without it those checks are silently absent.
