function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

arguments.content:
module WordTrie

export Trie, count_prefix

mutable struct Node
    children::Dict{Char,Node}
    count::Int
    terminal::Bool
end
Node() = Node(Dict{Char,Node}(), 0, false)

struct Trie
    root::Node
end
Trie() = Trie(Node())

Base.length(t::Trie) = t.root.count

function Base.push!(t::Trie, word::AbstractString)
    node = t.root
    node.count += 1
    for c in word
        node = get!(Node, node.children, c)
        node.count += 1
    end
    node.terminal = true
    return t
end

function _find(t::Trie, s::AbstractString)
    node = t.root
    for c in s
        node = get(node.children, c, nothing)
        isnothing(node) && return nothing
    end
    return node
end

function Base.in(word::AbstractString, t::Trie)
    node = _find(t, word)
    return !isnothing(node) && node.terminal
end

function count_prefix(t::Trie, prefix::AbstractString)
    node = _find(t, prefix)
    return isnothing(node) ? 0 : node.count
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. module SemverOrder

export SemVer, parse_semver

struct SemVer
    major::Int
    minor::Int
    patch::Int
    pre::Vector{String}
    build::Vector{String}
end

const IDENT = "[0-9A-Za-z-]+"
const SEMVER_RE = Regex("^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:-($IDENT(?:\\.$IDENT)*))?(?:\\+($IDENT(?:\\.$IDENT)*))?\$")

function parse_semver(str::AbstractString)
    m = match(SEMVER_RE, str)
    isnothing(m) && throw(ArgumentError("invalid semantic version: '$str'"))
    pre = isnothing(m[4]) ? String[] : String.(split(m[4], '.'))
    build = isnothing(m[5]) ? String[] : String.(split(m[5], '.'))
    return SemVer(parse(Int, m[1]), parse(Int, m[2]), parse(Int, m[3]), pre, build)
end

_isnum(s) = all(isdigit, s)

function _pre_isless(a::Vector{String}, b::Vector{String})
    isempty(a) && return false
    isempty(b) && return true
    for (x, y) in zip(a, b)
        x == y && continue
        return x < y
    end
    return length(a) < length(b)
end

function Base.isless(a::SemVer, b::SemVer)
    ka = (a.major, a.minor, a.patch)
    kb = (b.major, b.minor, b.patch)
    ka == kb || return ka < kb
    return _pre_isless(a.pre, b.pre)
end

end

@testitem "semver.org precedence chain" begin
    chain = ["1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-alpha.beta", "1.0.0-beta",
             "1.0.0-beta.2", "1.0.0-beta.11", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0", "2.0.0", "2.1.0", "2.1.1"]
    vs = parse_semver.(chain)
    for i in 1:length(vs)-1
        @test vs[i] < vs[i+1]
    end
    @test sort(reverse(vs)) == vs
end

@testitem "build metadata is ignored, parsing is strict" begin
    a, b = parse_semver("1.2.3+abc"), parse_semver("1.2.3+xyz")
    @test !(a < b) && !(b < a)
    @test parse_semver("1.0.0-x.7.z.92+exp.sha.5114f85").pre == ["x", "7", "z", "92"]
    for bad in ["1.2", "01.2.3", "1.2.3-", "1.2.3-α", "v1.2.3", ""]
        @test_throws "invalid semantic version: '$bad'" parse_semver(bad)
    end
end

@testitem "random versions agree with a tuple-key reference" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(1)
    ident() = rand(rng, Bool) ? string(rand(rng, 0:30)) : rand(rng, ["alpha", "beta", "rc", "x-1"])
    function randver()
        pre = rand(rng, Bool) ? join([ident() for _ in 1:rand(rng, 1:3)], '.') : ""
        base = "$(rand(rng, 0:2)).$(rand(rng, 0:2)).$(rand(rng, 0:2))"
        isempty(pre) ? base : base * "-" * pre
    end
    key(s) = begin
        core, _, pre = partition_pre(s)
        (core, isempty(pre) ? 1 : 0, [all(isdigit, p) ? (0, parse(Int, p), "") : (1, 0, p) for p in pre])
    end
    partition_pre(s) = begin
        c, _, p = partition(s, '-')
        (Tuple(parse.(Int, split(c, '.'))), nothing, isempty(p) ? String[] : String.(split(p, '.')))
    end
    partition(s, ch) = begin
        i = findfirst(ch, s)
        isnothing(i) ? (s, ch, "") : (s[1:prevind(s, i)], ch, s[nextind(s, i):end])
    end
    strs = [randver() for _ in 1:300]
    @test sort(strs; by = parse_semver) == sort(strs; by = key)
end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module BracketCheck

export balanced

function balanced(s::AbstractString)
    open_for = Dict(')' => '(', ']' => '[', '}' => '{')
    stack = Char[]
    for i in 1:length(s)
        c = s[i]
        if c in "([{"
            push!(stack, c)
        elseif haskey(open_for, c)
            (isempty(stack) || pop!(stack) != open_for[c]) && return false
        end
    end
    return isempty(stack)
end

end

`balanced` in `/work/Project/BracketCheck/src/BracketCheck.jl`:

```julia
module BracketCheck

export balanced

function balanced(s::AbstractString)
    open_for = Dict(')' => '(', ']' => '[', '}' => '{')
    stack = Char[]
    for c in s
        if c in "([{"
            push!(stack, c)
        elseif haskey(open_for, c)
            (isempty(stack) || pop!(stack) != open_for[c]) && return false
        end
    end
    return isempty(stack)
end

end
```

Not verified: very long strings (the oracle is quadratic, so the property test uses length at most 12), performance of `balanced` itself.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module RomanNum

export to_roman, from_roman

const TABLE = [1000 => "M", 900 => "CM", 500 => "D", 400 => "CD", 100 => "C", 90 => "XC",
               50 => "L", 40 => "XL", 10 => "X", 9 => "IX", 5 => "V", 4 => "IV", 1 => "I"]
const VALUE = Dict('I' => 1, 'V' => 5, 'X' => 10, 'L' => 50, 'C' => 100, 'D' => 500, 'M' => 1000)

function to_roman(n::Integer)
    1 <= n <= 3999 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot write $n as a Roman numeral (need 1 to 3999)"))
    io = IOBuffer()
    for (v, s) in TABLE
        while n >= v
            print(io, s)
            n -= v
        end
    end
    return String(take!(io))
end

function from_roman(s::AbstractString)
    n = sum((get(VALUE, c, 0) for c in s); init = 0)
    (1 <= n <= 3999 && to_roman(n) == s) || throw(ArgumentError("invalid Roman numeral: '$s'"))
    return n
end

end

`to_roman` and `from_roman` are in `/work/Project/RomanNum/src/RomanNum.jl`; all 14 test assertions pass.

The first run had 3 errors: `from_roman("IV")` and `from_roman("MCMXCIV")` threw "invalid Roman numeral", and so did the round trip. The cause was summing the symbol values without the subtractive rule, so "IV" became 6 and failed the canonical-form check. A smaller symbol before a larger one is now subtracted.

Verified:
- `to_roman(4) == "IV"`, `to_roman(1994) == "MCMXCIV"`, `to_roman(3999) == "MMMCMXCIX"`.
- `from_roman(to_roman(n)) == n` for every n in 1:3999.
- "IIII", "VX", "iv", "", "IC", "MMMM", "Ⅳ" (U+2163) and "XIIX" throw an `ArgumentError` quoting the input; `to_roman(0)` and `to_roman(4000)` throw an `ArgumentError`.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module KMerge

export merge_sorted

function merge_sorted(lists::AbstractVector{<:AbstractVector})
    pos = ones(Int, length(lists))
    out = similar(first(lists), 0)
    for _ in 1:sum(length, lists)
        best = 0
        for i in eachindex(lists)
            pos[i] <= length(lists[i]) || continue
            if best == 0 || lists[i][pos[i]] < lists[best][pos[best]]
                best = i
            end
        end
        push!(out, lists[best][pos[best]])
        pos[best] += 1
    end
    return out
end

end

Verified (last run above): two hand-written cases and 1000 random inputs (0-5 lists of length 0-6, values 0-9, so many ties and empty lists) match `sort(vcat(lists...))`.

The first version crashed on an empty outer vector (`first(lists)` is a BoundsError there); both the hand-written empty case and the random cases showed it.

Not verified: outer vectors that are not 1-based (`pos` is a plain 1-based vector indexed with `eachindex(lists)`, so an OffsetArray of lists would break), element types other than `Int`, stability of equal elements across lists, performance (it is O(total * k) by design).

module SnakeCase

export snake_case

function snake_case(s::AbstractString)
    io = IOBuffer()
    for c in s
        if isuppercase(c)
            position(io) > 0 && print(io, '_')
            print(io, lowercase(c))
        elseif c == ' ' || c == '-'
            print(io, '_')
        else
            print(io, c)
        end
    end
    return replace(String(take!(io)), r"_+" => "_")
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. I rewrote `standardize` as `standardize!` in /work/Project/src/std.jl to use less memory. Check that it does and tell me by how much for 10^6 elements.

using Statistics

standardize(x) = (x .- mean(x)) ./ std(x)

function standardize!(x)
    m = mean(x)
    s = std(x; mean = m)
    x .= (x .- m) ./ s
    return x
end

y = standardize(x)
z = standardize!(copy(x))

messages.content:
The in-place version allocates far less per call. From the tool output above, for 10^6 `Float64` elements (the input itself is 8000000 bytes), `@allocated` reported 8000072 bytes for `standardize` and 0 bytes for `standardize!`. Both returned the same values (`y ≈ z` was `true`).

The code, from `src/std.jl`:

```julia
using Statistics

standardize(x) = (x .- mean(x)) ./ std(x)

function standardize!(x)
    m = mean(x)
    s = std(x; mean = m)
    x .= (x .- m) ./ s
    return x
end
```

Scope of the claim: `@allocated` counts bytes allocated during one call. It is not the process's peak memory or resident set size, and I did not measure either. It also covers only this one input size and one call each, after warm-up. `standardize!` overwrites its input, so if the caller needs the original, the copy has to be paid for outside the function.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module QueryParse

export parse_query, encode_component

function decode_component(s::AbstractString)
    out = IOBuffer()
    i = firstindex(s)
    while i <= lastindex(s)
        c = s[i]
        if c == '+'
            print(out, ' ')
        elseif c == '%'
            hex = SubString(s, nextind(s, i), min(lastindex(s), nextind(s, i, 2)))
            length(hex) == 2 && all(isxdigit, hex) ||
                throw(ArgumentError("malformed percent escape in '$s'"))
            print(out, Char(parse(UInt8, hex; base = 16)))
            i = nextind(s, i, 2)
        else
            print(out, c)
        end
        i = nextind(s, i)
    end
    return String(take!(out))
end

function parse_query(s::AbstractString)
    result = Dict{String,Vector{String}}()
    for piece in split(s, '&'; keepempty = false)
        k, v = occursin('=', piece) ? split(piece, '='; limit = 2) : (piece, "")
        push!(get!(Vector{String}, result, decode_component(k)), decode_component(v))
    end
    return result
end

function encode_component(s::AbstractString)
    out = IOBuffer()
    for b in codeunits(s)
        c = Char(b)
        if isascii(c) && (isletter(c) || isdigit(c) || c in "-_.~")
            print(out, c)
        else
            print(out, '%', uppercase(string(b, base = 16, pad = 2)))
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out))
end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

This is a prerequisite for every other Julia workspace tool — julia_get_diagnostics, julia_format_file, julia_list_testitems and julia_run_testitems all fail until it has been called. Parses the Julia source under each folder, resolves the Project.toml/Manifest.toml environments, and detects @testitem and @testsetup blocks. Julia sessions (julia_create_session) are separate and need no workspace.

function.description: Report Julia syntax errors, lint warnings and test item detection errors, for the whole workspace or a single file. tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs (case-insensitive).

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Re-run only the failed and errored Julia test items from an earlier run, reusing that run's settings. Returns a new test run id; the original run is left intact. function.name: mcp_julia_julia_rerun_failed

timeout.description: Per-item timeout override.

max_workers.description: Max workers override.

max_wait_seconds.description: Override for how long this call waits before returning the run as still running (default 600).

testrun_id.description: ID of the previous test run whose failures to re-run.

memory_threshold.description: Worker recycle threshold override.

function.description: Stop an in-progress Julia test run — typically one julia_run_testitems handed back with status "running" because it outlasted max_wait_seconds, or one that turned out to be hanging. testrun_id.description: ID of the test run to cancel.

function.description: Get the summary and per-item status lines for a Julia test run, whether it has completed or is still going — this is the tool to poll after julia_run_testitems returned with status "running". function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testrun_results

include_passing.description: Include passing test items in results (default: false).

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Get the full result of one or more Julia test items: failure messages, stack traces, and captured output (stdout and stderr interleaved). function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testitem_detail

testitem_ids.description: Test item ids to inspect. Unknown ids are reported per item rather than failing the call.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on captured output per item (default 8000). The tail is kept; read the testrun://{id}/items/{id}/output resource for the full stream.

max_messages.description: Cap on failure messages per item (default 20).

testrun_id.description: Test run ID.

testitem_id.description: Single test item id. Prefer testitem_ids for more than one.

max_stack_frames.description: Cap on stack frames per message (default 20).

function.description: List every Julia test run this server has started, with status and pass/fail counts. Use it to recover a testrun_id for julia_get_testrun_results, julia_get_testitem_detail or julia_rerun_failed — including when a julia_run_testitems call was interrupted or its result went missing. function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_testruns

function.description: List the Julia worker processes currently held for running test items. They persist between runs by design — that is what makes repeat runs fast. function.description: Kill a Julia test worker process. Its loaded packages and compiled code are lost, so the next run needing it pays full Julia startup and precompilation again. Only worth doing when a worker is wedged or Revise cannot apply a change — editing a struct definition, for instance.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_terminate_test_process

function.description: Get line-level Julia code coverage for a test run. Only available for runs started with mode="Coverage"; anything else returns an error.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_coverage_results

testrun_id.description: Test run ID (must have been run with mode="Coverage").

function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. State — variables, functions, loaded packages, compiled code — survives across julia_eval_code calls, so iterating inside one session avoids paying Julia's startup and compilation cost over and over. Prefer this over shelling out to `julia -e` for anything beyond a single throwaway command. Revise is loaded, so edits made to package source on disk take effect on the next evaluation without a restart. Sessions are independent of the analysis workspace: julia_set_workspace_folders is not required. The response echoes the resolved environment; pass it back here to replace a session that died.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_create_session

use_test_env.description: Activate the package's test environment via TestEnv (default false).

project.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the project to activate. Omitted means Julia's default environment.

package.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the package being developed, when there is one.

env.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes the variable.

package_name.description: Name of the package being developed.

julia_cmd.description: Path to the Julia executable (default: the one running this server).

function.description: Evaluate Julia code in a persistent session and return the value, captured output, and any error. A Julia exception comes back as a normal result with status "error" rather than a tool failure, so the message and backtrace are there to read. Definitions and variables persist for later calls in the same session. Revise runs first by default, so edits made to package source on disk are picked up before the code runs.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_eval_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the evaluation is interrupted. Omit for no timeout; Julia precompilation can take minutes.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on returned output, keeping the tail (default 8000).

revise.description: Run Revise first so edits made on disk take effect (default true).

session_id.description: Session to evaluate in, from julia_create_session.

code.description: Julia code to evaluate. Multiple top-level statements are allowed; the value of the last one is returned.

function.description: Interrupt whatever a Julia session is currently evaluating, as Ctrl-C would. Queued requests are discarded and the session stays alive and usable. Julia code that never yields (`while true; end`, or a long call into a C library) may not be interruptible, especially on Windows — julia_kill_session is the only recourse there.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_interrupt_session

function.description: Terminate a Julia session and discard all of its state. There is no restart tool: to start over with the same setup, call julia_create_session with the environment julia_list_sessions reports for it.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_kill_session

function.description: List the Julia sessions this server manages, with each one's status and the environment it was created with. That environment is what julia_create_session needs to recreate a session after julia_kill_session.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_sessions

function.description: Profile Julia code in a session and return the hottest functions by self and total sample count. Use kind="alloc" for an allocation profile instead of CPU sampling. Run the code once with julia_eval_code first — otherwise compilation dominates the samples and the profile says nothing useful.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_profile_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the profile run is interrupted.

max_entries.description: Number of hot functions to report (default 25).

code.description: Julia code to profile. Run it once first so compilation does not dominate the profile.

function.description: List the bindings of a module in a Julia session with rendered values — the equivalent of a debugger's variable pane. Values too expensive to render eagerly come back with lazy=true and an id; pass that id back as variable_id to expand that value's children.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_session_variables

include_modules.description: Include module bindings in the listing (default false).

variable_id.description: Expand the children of this lazily reported variable instead of listing a module.

You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- Additional docs: /usr/lib/node_modules/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs

- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing

module QuickSelect

export kth_smallest

function kth_smallest(v::AbstractVector, k::Integer)
    a = collect(v)
    lo, hi = 1, length(a)
    while true
        p = a[(lo + hi) >> 1]
        i, j = lo, hi
        while i <= j
            while a[i] < p
                i += 1
            end
            while a[j] > p
                j -= 1
            end
            if i <= j
                a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
                i += 1
                j -= 1
            end
        end
        if k <= j
            hi = j
        elseif k >= i
            lo = i
        else
            return a[k]
        end
    end
end

end

`kth_smallest` in `/work/Project/QuickSelect/src/QuickSelect.jl`:

```julia
module QuickSelect

export kth_smallest

function kth_smallest(v::AbstractVector, k::Integer)
    1 <= k <= length(v) || throw(ArgumentError("k = $k is outside 1:$(length(v))"))
    a = collect(v)
    lo, hi = 1, length(a)
    while true
        p = a[(lo + hi) >> 1]
        i, j = lo, hi
        while i <= j
            while a[i] < p
                i += 1
            end
            while a[j] > p
                j -= 1
            end
            if i <= j
                a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
                i += 1
                j -= 1
            end
        end
        if k <= j
            hi = j
        elseif k >= i
            lo = i
        else
            return a[k]
        end
    end
end

end
```

Verified (last run above): 2000 random vectors with many duplicates (values in -5:5, length 1-15) match `sort(v)[k]` for a random k, `v` is left unmodified, and `k = 0` and `k = 4` on a 3-element vector throw `ArgumentError`.

My first version had no range check. The first run printed the `k = 0` BoundsError and then had to be interrupted at the 30 second cap; the call after it is `k = 4`. That the `k = 4` call is the one that looped is my inference from where the run stopped; I did not run it in isolation.

Not verified: OffsetArray input (`collect` makes a 1-based copy, so it should work, but I did not test it), non-numeric element types, speed against `sort`.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

coverage_root_uris.description: Deprecated and ignored: coverage is always collected for the packages under test.

name_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against test item names.

package.description: Filter to items in this package only.

items.description: Specific test item ids to run, as reported by julia_list_testitems. If omitted, runs all (or filtered) items.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Re-run only the failed and errored Julia test items from an earlier run, reusing that run's settings. Returns a new test run id; the original run is left intact. The usual loop is julia_run_testitems, fix the code, then this — the worker processes pick up the fix via Revise. Waits up to max_wait_seconds like julia_run_testitems and returns early with status "running" the same way.

timeout.description: Per-item timeout override.

max_workers.description: Max workers override.

max_wait_seconds.description: Override for how long this call waits before returning the run as still running (default 600).

testrun_id.description: ID of the previous test run whose failures to re-run.

memory_threshold.description: Worker recycle threshold override.

function.description: Stop an in-progress Julia test run — typically one julia_run_testitems handed back with status "running" because it outlasted max_wait_seconds, or one that turned out to be hanging. function.name: mcp_julia_julia_cancel_testrun

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run to cancel.

function.description: Get the summary and per-item status lines for a Julia test run, whether it has completed or is still going — this is the tool to poll after julia_run_testitems returned with status "running". It returns immediately with the current state; the run is done once status is no longer "running". Same compact shape julia_run_testitems returns — use julia_get_testitem_detail for failure messages, stack traces and captured output. Durations are milliseconds; the summary duration is elapsed wall-clock time, and for a run still in progress it is the time elapsed so far.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testrun_results

include_passing.description: Include passing test items in results (default: false).

testrun_id.description: ID of the test run.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

function.description: Get the full result of one or more Julia test items: failure messages, stack traces, and captured output (stdout and stderr interleaved). This is the follow-up to julia_run_testitems — pass every id you want to inspect in a single call rather than one call per item. Supply testitem_ids or testitem_id; at least one is required. If a whole worker process died before running anything (a precompilation error, say), the cause is in the testprocess://{process_id}/output resource instead.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_testitem_detail

testitem_ids.description: Test item ids to inspect. Unknown ids are reported per item rather than failing the call.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on captured output per item (default 8000). The tail is kept; read the testrun://{id}/items/{id}/output resource for the full stream.

max_messages.description: Cap on failure messages per item (default 20).

testrun_id.description: Test run ID.

testitem_id.description: Single test item id. Prefer testitem_ids for more than one.

max_stack_frames.description: Cap on stack frames per message (default 20).

function.description: List every Julia test run this server has started, with status and pass/fail counts. Use it to recover a testrun_id for julia_get_testrun_results, julia_get_testitem_detail or julia_rerun_failed — including when a julia_run_testitems call was interrupted or its result went missing. Runs that outlasted max_wait_seconds show as "running" until they finish or are cancelled.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_testruns

function.description: List the Julia worker processes currently held for running test items. They persist between runs by design — that is what makes repeat runs fast. Read the testprocess://{process_id}/output resource for a process's raw output, which is where precompilation and startup failures show up.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_test_processes

function.description: Kill a Julia test worker process. Its loaded packages and compiled code are lost, so the next run needing it pays full Julia startup and precompilation again. Only worth doing when a worker is wedged or Revise cannot apply a change — editing a struct definition, for instance.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_terminate_test_process

function.description: Get line-level Julia code coverage for a test run. Only available for runs started with mode="Coverage"; anything else returns an error.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_coverage_results

testrun_id.description: Test run ID (must have been run with mode="Coverage").

function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. State — variables, functions, loaded packages, compiled code — survives across julia_eval_code calls, so iterating inside one session avoids paying Julia's startup and compilation cost over and over. Prefer this over shelling out to `julia -e` for anything beyond a single throwaway command. Revise is loaded, so edits made to package source on disk take effect on the next evaluation without a restart. Sessions are independent of the analysis workspace: julia_set_workspace_folders is not required. The response echoes the resolved environment; pass it back here to replace a session that died.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_create_session

use_test_env.description: Activate the package's test environment via TestEnv (default false).

project.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the project to activate. Omitted means Julia's default environment.

package.description: Absolute path or file:// URI of the package being developed, when there is one.

env.description: Environment variable overrides. A null value removes the variable.

package_name.description: Name of the package being developed.

julia_cmd.description: Path to the Julia executable (default: the one running this server).

function.description: Evaluate Julia code in a persistent session and return the value, captured output, and any error. A Julia exception comes back as a normal result with status "error" rather than a tool failure, so the message and backtrace are there to read. Definitions and variables persist for later calls in the same session. Revise runs first by default, so edits made to package source on disk are picked up before the code runs.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_eval_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the evaluation is interrupted. Omit for no timeout; Julia precompilation can take minutes.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on returned output, keeping the tail (default 8000).

revise.description: Run Revise first so edits made on disk take effect (default true).

session_id.description: Session to evaluate in, from julia_create_session.

code.description: Julia code to evaluate. Multiple top-level statements are allowed; the value of the last one is returned.

function.description: Interrupt whatever a Julia session is currently evaluating, as Ctrl-C would. Queued requests are discarded and the session stays alive and usable. Julia code that never yields (`while true; end`, or a long call into a C library) may not be interruptible, especially on Windows — julia_kill_session is the only recourse there.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_interrupt_session

function.description: Terminate a Julia session and discard all of its state. There is no restart tool: to start over with the same setup, call julia_create_session with the environment julia_list_sessions reports for it.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_kill_session

function.description: List the Julia sessions this server manages, with each one's status and the environment it was created with. That environment is what julia_create_session needs to recreate a session after julia_kill_session.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_list_sessions

function.description: Profile Julia code in a session and return the hottest functions by self and total sample count. Use kind="alloc" for an allocation profile instead of CPU sampling. Run the code once with julia_eval_code first — otherwise compilation dominates the samples and the profile says nothing useful.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_profile_code

timeout.description: Seconds before the profile run is interrupted.

max_entries.description: Number of hot functions to report (default 25).

code.description: Julia code to profile. Run it once first so compilation does not dominate the profile.

function.description: List the bindings of a module in a Julia session with rendered values — the equivalent of a debugger's variable pane. Values too expensive to render eagerly come back with lazy=true and an id; pass that id back as variable_id to expand that value's children.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_get_session_variables

include_modules.description: Include module bindings in the listing (default false).

variable_id.description: Expand the children of this lazily reported variable instead of listing a module.

- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

arguments.content:
module Knapsack01

export knapsack

function knapsack(weights::AbstractVector{<:Integer}, values::AbstractVector{<:Real}, capacity::Integer)
    axes(weights) == axes(values) ||
        throw(DimensionMismatch("weights and values must have the same axes, got $(axes(weights)) and $(axes(values))"))
    capacity >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("capacity must be nonnegative, got $capacity"))
    all(>(0), weights) || throw(ArgumentError("weights must be positive"))
    best = zeros(eltype(values), capacity + 1)
    for i in eachindex(weights)
        w, v = weights[i], values[i]
        for c in capacity:-1:w
            best[c + 1] = max(best[c + 1], best[c + 1 - w] + v)
        end
    end
    return best[end]
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
